units: Unified framework studying intelligence as capacity to convert feedback into increased future viability.
I is proposed proportional to C_improve.
C_improve is capacity to convert feedback into increased future viability.
Intelligence is proposed to include improvement of mechanisms responsible for future adaptation, not only optimization within fixed structure.
Reality -> Representation -> Reachability -> Correction -> Adaptation -> Improved Representation; R -> Omega -> C -> A -> R'.
R: internal models and compressed structures extracted from reality.
Omega: grounded reachability, the future states the system can actually influence.
C: correction capacity, the ability of reality to modify the system through feedback.
A: ability to update strategies, representations and mechanisms.
R': a more capable internal model after adaptation.
Can adaptive systems improve the representation space and mechanisms through which future improvements occur, not only parameters?
REE proposal: G_(t+1)=F(G_t,E_t), with G written as reachable adaptive mechanism space.
REE proposes that the system can modify the space of transformations available to it.
External reality must retain causal access to the mechanism of future change.
Without continued causal access, optimization and capability can increase while correction disappears and the system becomes disconnected from its selecting environment.
Framework is explored through multiple connected projects covering representation evolution, adaptive transition, recursive adaptation, and stability/correction.
Recursive Representation Expansion is source-mapped to repository slug `ree` and described as testing representation expansion under environmental pressure.
Endpoint identity not resolved by parser.
Causal Transition & Representation Evolution is source-mapped to `ctre_simulator` and described as studying transition from fixed optimization toward reality-coupled self-revision.
Endpoint identity not resolved by parser.
Recursive Adaptive Dynamics is source-mapped to `recursive-adaptive-dynamics` and described as studying modification of mechanisms that generate future capabilities.
Endpoint identity not resolved by parser.
Adaptive Stability Framework is source-mapped to `adaptive-stability-framework` and described as measuring correction preservation, divergence and stability of self-updating systems.
Endpoint identity not resolved by parser.
Interface-Induced Computational Geometry is source-described as a foundation in which interfaces determine computational space available to bounded agents.
Computational Phase Boundaries is source-described as addressing capability jumps when new computational regions become reachable.
Resolution Horizon is source-described as measuring limits from information, representation, computation and observation.
Representation Elasticity is source-described as studying representation change as a driver of discovery and efficiency.
Computational Leverage is source-described as measuring disproportionate capability gains from representation changes.
A successful adaptive system must preserve reality-driven correction.
Objective is framed as maximum generative capacity that remains beneficial after the system's own removal, not maximum power.
A system succeeds when residual capability remains after the system itself is gone.
Source states the theoretical framework is developed and multiple formal models have been proposed.
Source states proof-of-concept simulators are implemented.
Program-level status; no implementation path exists in R25 frozen head.
Source states experimental validation is in progress.
Goal is to identify structural conditions under which adaptive systems begin modifying their own future learning capabilities.
No scale, estimator, intervention protocol, or units are defined for C_improve or future viability; proportionality constant/domain for I proportional to C_improve is unspecified.
Grounded reachability Omega, correction capacity C, adaptation A and criterion for R' being improved are conceptual definitions without operational estimators here.
Reachable adaptive mechanism space G and the update F(G,E) are not operationally defined; expansion versus ordinary parameter/feature update is not given a decision rule.
E*, C_rev and the causal-access arrow are not operationalized or identified by an intervention/estimation protocol.
Literal repository slugs and named frameworks are source references; immutable corpus endpoint identity is not resolved at parse stage and no edge is emitted.
Generative capacity, benefit after removal, and residual capability lack measurement, baseline, horizon and causal-attribution protocols in this file.

Claims that proof-of-concept simulators are implemented and validation is in progress refer to broader program status; R25 frozen head contains no simulator, benchmark run, result artifact or implementation lineage.
Unified research program investigating transition from fixed optimization to reality-coupled recursive self-improvement.
I is proposed proportional to C_improve.
I denotes intelligence; C_improve denotes capacity to convert environmental feedback into increased future viability.
Intelligence is proposed as recursive improvement of future adaptive capacity rather than optimization performance alone.
Core loop Reality -> R -> Omega -> C -> A -> R', feeding REE and reachable adaptive mechanism space G.
Structural-constraint layer names Causal Permeability Principle, Constitutional Correction Capacity, Grounded Recursive Adaptation, Adaptive Stability Framework and Alignment Spine.

Computational-foundation layer names Interface-Induced Computational Geometry, Representation Elasticity, Computational Leverage, Computational Phase Boundary, Resolution Horizon and Computational Resolution Horizon.
Experimental-program layer names REE, CTRE, RAD and Representation Phase Benchmark.
Reality -> Representation -> Reachability -> Correction -> Adaptation -> Improved Representation; R -> Omega -> C -> A -> R'.
R extracts structure into an internal model; Omega is futures the system can influence; C is reality-driven correction; A updates representations, strategies and mechanisms; R' begins the next cycle.
Traditional learning optimizes within fixed representational space; REE proposes modifying the representational space itself.
G is reachable adaptive mechanism space and E environmental feedback.
System is proposed to expand mechanisms available for future adaptation.
Central condition: E* is linked by a causal/corrigibility arrow to C_rev.
External reality must retain causal access to the mechanism responsible for future change.
Optimization may continue while adaptive quality diverges from reality if correction is lost.
Program is organized into core mechanism, structural constraints, computational foundations and experimental systems.
Core mechanism names Recursive Representation Expansion.
Structural constraints repeat Causal Permeability Principle, Constitutional Correction Capacity, Grounded Recursive Adaptation, Adaptive Stability Framework and Alignment Spine.

Computational foundations repeat Interface-Induced Computational Geometry, Representation Elasticity, Computational Leverage, Computational Phase Boundary, Resolution Horizon, Computational Resolution Horizon and add Adaptive Metric Compiler.
Experimental systems name REE Simulator, CTRE Simulator, Recursive Adaptive Dynamics and Representation Phase Benchmark.

How do adaptive systems transition from fixed optimization to reality-coupled recursive self-improvement? Subquestions concern self-modifying adaptive mechanisms, preservation of correction, representation effects on computational reach, and measurable/reproducible recursive adaptation.
Source claims formal theoretical framework, multiple connected mathematical models, proof-of-concept simulators, experimental benchmarks and open-source implementations.
Program-level claim; current R25 head contains documents only.
Long-term objective is a unified theory of how adaptive systems generate, preserve and recursively improve future capability.
I proportional to C_improve remains uncalibrated and C_improve/future viability lacks an estimator or common scale.
The diagram asserts layer ordering and module placement but does not provide empirical evidence that these layers are causally ordered or exhaustive.
G, F and criteria distinguishing mechanism-space expansion from ordinary update remain operationally unspecified in this repository.
E*, C_rev and causal-access relation lack intervention semantics, estimator and threshold in this source.
Named modules/simulators/frameworks are not bound here to immutable corpus repository heads; recurrence and names do not license endpoint identity or program edges.
Claims of simulators, benchmarks and open-source implementations are not evidenced by implementation/result artifacts in R25's five-file frozen head.
